text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, six activities that each ran in roughly half of the cases before now run in almost every case: A33, A35 and A36 rose from about 49 to about 98–99 in 100 traces, and A37, A38 and A39 from about 52 to about 99–100 in 100. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]

- Before, the two triples were mutually exclusive: A33 and A37, for example, appeared together in only about 1–2 in 100 traces while each appeared without the other in roughly half; within each triple the activities always came together. In the later window, every cross-triple pair co-occurs in about 98 in 100 traces, with A33/A35/A36 preceding A37/A38/A39 in about 95–98 in 100 of those; order inside each triple is mixed, with both directions close to even. [REL039, REL041, REL045, REL047, REL050, REL052, REL037, REL044, REL055, REL059]

- The combined set sits between A30 and A31: A30 precedes A33/A35/A36 in about 95–98 in 100 later-window traces, and A33/A35/A36 precede A31 in about 95–97 in 100. Distances grew as expected if three activities were inserted: the A30→A37/A38/A39 and A33/A35/A36→A31 gaps moved from about 1–3 steps to 4–5 steps, and the A30→A31 pair within five steps — present in about 199 of 200 before-traces, mostly 4 steps apart — appears in only about 5 later traces. A30's mean position is slightly earlier (about 0.67 to 0.62 of the trace) and A31's slightly later (about 0.80 to 0.82). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL025, REL027, REL031, REL033, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG009, LAG011, LAG013, POS003, POS004]

- A04 appears in far fewer cases (about 59 to about 26 in 100 traces) and, when it does, later in the trace (mean position about 0.20 to 0.38). The step out of A14 changed: A04's share of A14's outgoing transitions fell from about 57% to about 12% while A15's rose from about 43% to about 79%, and A14-before-A04 fell from about 55 to about 18 in 100 traces. A04 also now rarely appears without the block activities: for A04 and A33, traces with A04 but not A33 fell from about 31 to about 2 in 100, while A33-alone rose from about 21 to about 75 in 100. A14 and A15 themselves still occur in every trace in both windows. [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, DIR004, REL001, REL005, POS002]

- A02, A08 and A10 participate more often (about 6 to 18, 8 to 18 and 6 to 23 in 100 traces respectively); A02 and A10 also exit to a wider set of successors (A10 from about 9 to about 23 distinct targets, A48 taking about 22%). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]

- Smaller shifts: A47 still usually precedes A48 but less exclusively (about 97% to 84% of A47's outgoing, with about 15 in 100 pairs now two steps apart versus 3–4 before), and A45→A46 weakened similarly (about 96% to 82%). [DIR009, DIR010, LAG015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two mutually exclusive groups of three activities were replaced by both groups executing in sequence in every case: before, a trace typically ran A30, then either A33–A35–A36 or A37–A38–A39 (each in about half the cases, essentially never both), then A31; in the later window it typically runs A30, then A33/A35/A36 in varying order, then A37/A38/A39 in varying order, then A31. The change is shown directly by relational evidence — cross-group co-occurrence rising from about 1–2 to about 98 in 100 with consistent precedence — and corroborated by successor shares (exits from A33, A35 and A36 to A31 collapsing from about 27–34% to under 1%, replaced by continuations into the other group) and by lag distances that grow exactly as three inserted activities would predict. [REL039, REL045, REL050, REL037, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG009, OCC005, OCC008]

A second, separately visible difference is the rerouting around A04 — A14 now usually continues to A15 rather than A04, A04 appears in far fewer and later cases, and A02, A08 and A10 appear more often; the evidence shows these shifts directly but cannot establish whether they belong to the same structural difference as the group change. [DIR004, OCC002, POS001, DIR002, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003]

The windows are finite samples of 200 traces each, so a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants — for example a rare variant already running both groups, or running without A04, that was absent from the earlier window and dominant later — could produce the same picture without any modification to the process. Every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, which makes sampling noise unlikely but cannot by itself exclude a rare variant; moreover, many items restate one group-level change (the six occurrence profiles and the cross-group relations describe the same traces), so they are not independent confirmations, and a few lag profiles rest on very few observations (A30→A31 on about 5 later traces). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, REL039, REL045, REL050, LAG004]
